classification.difficultyReason: Place each centre on coordinate axes and use its radius to sketch the circle with the correct axis relationships, including tangency and a circle wholly within quadrant II.

content.prompt: Draw a sketch of each circle with the following features.

answer.short: Circle centred at $(0,0)$ with radius $2$, passing through $(\pm2,0)$ and $(0,\pm2)$.
answer.worked: Mark the centre $(0,0)$ and the points $(2,0)$, $(-2,0)$, $(0,2)$ and $(0,-2)$. Draw a circle through these points.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 2, referring to Question 1(a); answer book PDF page 31, bottom left
spec.description: Equal-scale axes and a circle centred at the origin; four extremes labelled as in the answer evidence. Decorative source blue is replaced by black.
spec.answerVisibility: Solution only; student receives blank sketch space.

answer.short: Circle centred at $(3,-2)$ with radius $2$, tangent to the $x$-axis at $(3,0)$.
answer.worked: Mark the centre $(3,-2)$. The left, right, upper and lower extremes are $(1,-2)$, $(5,-2)$, $(3,0)$ and $(3,-4)$. Draw the circle through these points.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 2, referring to Question 1(b); answer book PDF page 31, top right
spec.description: Equal-scale axes, circle tangent to the x-axis and dashed centre guides labelled 3 and -2. Decorative source blue is replaced by black.
spec.answerVisibility: Solution only; student receives blank sketch space.

answer.worked: Mark the centre $(-2,1)$. The horizontal extremes are $(-2-\sqrt3,1)$ and $(-2+\sqrt3,1)$; the vertical extremes are $(-2,1-\sqrt3)$ and $(-2,1+\sqrt3)$. Draw the circle through these points.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 2, referring to Question 1(c); answer book PDF page 31, right column
spec.description: Equal-scale axes, circle crossing the x-axis to the left of the y-axis and dashed centre guides labelled -2 and 1. Decorative source blue is replaced by black.
spec.answerVisibility: Solution only; student receives blank sketch space.

answer.short: Circle centred at $(-1,1)$ with radius $\frac14$, wholly in quadrant II.
answer.worked: Mark the centre $(-1,1)$. The horizontal extremes are $(-\frac54,1)$ and $(-\frac34,1)$; the vertical extremes are $(-1,\frac34)$ and $(-1,\frac54)$. Draw the circle through these points.
